transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've been informed that our normal polymer resin shipment is delayed, but we have 210 kilograms of the normal resin and 90 kilograms of an alternate resin lot available in the warehouse. I also understand the injection-molding line is idle and could produce 600 housings tomorrow if we authorize the alternate material. Since this would be a non-routine material run, I need to follow our pre-run authorization routine — which means I need both a materials review and a compliance review before I can make a decision. Can someone walk me through the materials review for this alternate resin?

transcript.text: I need to share the results of my compatibility trial. I completed a trial that's recorded in my lab notebook: the alternate resin is qualified only at exactly 30% alternate resin blended with 70% normal resin, and the combined material must be dried for exactly 4 hours at 80 degrees Celsius. I have not yet copied this trial result into the production order. The good news is that our available inventory of 210 kilograms of normal resin and 90 kilograms of alternate resin matches this exact 70/30 blend ratio.

transcript.text: Elena, I've completed my compliance review for this alternate-resin run. My customer deviation review — which is based on an approval email that has not yet been entered into the quality system — permits exactly 600 housings from this alternate-resin run. The deviation requires that exactly 12 first-off units receive dimensional inspection, and that serialized lot traceability is maintained for every released housing. These controls will need to be recorded in the production order before the run is released.
